title: Composition into a finite projective space over an affine base
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X\xrightarrow f Y\xrightarrow g S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that $f$ and $g$ each admit a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over their respective target; a locally closed immersion means a closed immersion into an open subscheme of the target [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Then there are $N\geq0$ and a locally closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ whose composite with projection is $g\circ f$.

source.place: Tag 0C4M (lemma-composition-quasi-projective), followed by Tag 01VT (lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample), over the affine base.

proof.text: Choose integers $a,b\geq0$ and immersions $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^a_Y$ and $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^b_S$ supplied by the two hypotheses. Write $p_Y:\mathbf P^a_Y\to Y$, $p_A:\mathbf P^a_S\to S$ and $p_B:\mathbf P^b_S\to S$ for the structure maps. Thus $p_Y\circ i=f$ and $p_B\circ j=g$. The notation for projective spaces is [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with the coordinate index sets $\{0,\ldots,a\}$ and $\{0,\ldots,b\}$. Immersion has exactly the closed-then-open meaning of [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 01NF (definition-projective-space); unpacking the two immersion hypotheses.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] for $g:Y\to S$, identify $\mathbf P^a_Y$ with $Y\times_S\mathbf P^a_S$ over $Y$, and let $u:\mathbf P^a_Y\to\mathbf P^a_S$ be its second projection. Put $T=\mathbf P^b_S\times_S\mathbf P^a_S$, with projections $r_B,r_A$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $k=(j\circ p_Y,u):\mathbf P^a_Y\to T$. The square with upper map $k$, lower map $j$, and vertical maps $p_Y,r_B$ is cartesian: a pair $v:W\to Y$, $t:W\to T$ with $j\circ v=r_B\circ t$ determines the unique pair $(v,r_A\circ t):W\to Y\times_S\mathbf P^a_S$; its compatibility follows from $g=p_B\circ j$ and $p_B\circ r_B=p_A\circ r_A$. Its image under $k$ equals $t$ because both projections agree. Conversely the two projections of any lift must be this pair. Thus $k$ is the base change of the immersion $j$ along $r_B$, so it is an immersion by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft].

source.place: Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), with projective space defined by base change in Constructions, Tag 01NF (definition-projective-space).

proof.text: The two maps $i$ and $k$ are immersions, so clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives an immersion $h=k\circ i:X\hookrightarrow T$. It lies over $g\circ f$: using the projection identities from the preceding steps, $(p_B\circ r_B)\circ h=p_B\circ j\circ p_Y\circ i=g\circ f$.

Apply [lem-chow-segre] with the ordered dimensions $b,a$ over the scheme $S$. It gives the Segre closed immersion $s:T=\mathbf P^b_S\times_S\mathbf P^a_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$, where $N=(b+1)(a+1)-1=ab+a+b\geq0$. A closed immersion is an immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion] (take the whole target as its open subscheme). Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] therefore shows that $s\circ h$ is an immersion. Since $s$ is an $S$-morphism and $(p_B\circ r_B)\circ h=g\circ f$, its composite with $\mathbf P^N_S\to S$ is exactly $g\circ f$. This is the required locally closed immersion.

proof_origin.place: Direct Segre proof assembled from Tags 01NF and 01WD and Schemes Tags 01JY and 02V0; proves the finite-projective-space version of the composition assertion cited in Morphisms Tag 0C4M.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: scheme quotient X double-prime/H, projectivity over X, and the prime-to-ell generic cover. Supporting input: passing from the stated quasi-projective base to one affine base before constructing the homogeneous quotient.

The direct Segre proof is labelled agent-written, which is accurate. Step 1 is elementary unpacking of the two immersions. Step 2: the pullback lemma gives u with p_A u = g p_Y, so k = (j p_Y, u) is defined. I re-checked the cartesian argument: the lift (v, r_A t) exists because g v = p_B r_B t = p_A r_A t, k sends it to t, and it is unique. So k is the base change of j along r_B, and clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft makes it an immersion. Step 3: clause (e) of lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence gives h = k∘i over g∘f. Step 4: lem-chow-segre with m=b, n=a gives the Segre closed immersion over S into P^{ab+a+b}_S, def-chow-segre makes it a morphism over the base, and clause (e) applies again. Every step uses statements only, with no cycle. Edge cases checked: a or b = 0, a = b = 0, X or Y empty, R = 0. Closest existing node is lem-trf-h-projective-composition, the closed-immersion version; it does not give the locally closed statement, so it is not a duplicate.
